messages:
Ryan: heads-up — p99 latency for shared-gpu pool C spiked from ~90ms to 650ms last night around 03:20 UTC, throughput dropped ~30% :grimacing:
Maya: saw that. traces show frequent kernel re-selection events and a surge in KV cache evictions for some tenants. looks like a single bursty tenant is thrashing the hot KV slots :eyes:
Ilya: I grabbed a quick perf dump from the runtime around the window. main anomalies:
- kernel_switch_count ↑ 4x
- avg_kernel_init_time ~ 18ms (was ~2ms)
- KVCache::evict_rate jumped to 82%
- batching queue depth oscillating (very short micro-batches then big ones)

Ilya: pasted the snippet from profiling tool:
```
[2026-02-14T03:20:11Z] tenant="acme-ux" seq=32 kernel=quant_fused init=17.8ms exec=1.9ms
[2026-02-14T03:20:12Z] tenant="acme-ux" KVCache: miss -> eviction(78%) slots=512 active=490
[2026-02-14T03:20:12Z] tenant="acme-ux" batch_size=1 
[2026-02-14T03:20:12Z] kernel_switch: quant_fused -> fp16_transform (conflict on kernel selection)
```
Maya: that kernel flip is suspicious — our kernel selector seems to be oscillating when sequence lengths vary a lot mid-session. combined with extreme micro-batching, GPUs see constant re-upload/setup vs steady-stream ops.
Priya: is the tenant using mixed-precision variants or sending dynamic function calls? I recall a recent deploy that enabled dynamic-length packing for some customers.
Ryan: acme-ux is on a dev integration but they've been running a stress harness that sends alternating short/long sequences and occasional tool calls.
Devon: ops-bot shows they had a spike of concurrent sessions: 420 -> 1200 in 2m. probably caused KV cache pressure and forced evictions.
ops-bot: IncidentBot: alerted high-latency on shared-pool-C at 2026-02-14T03:20:08Z. Incident severity: P2.
Maya: immediate mitigation ideas:
- throttle per-tenant QPS on shared pools (soft cap + backoff)
- reserve KV cache partitions per-tenant or per-tier to prevent noisy eviction
- add hysteresis to kernel selector (avoid flip unless >X% benefit)
- tune batching heuristics to prefer slightly larger stable batches over micro-batches under oscillation

Ilya: confirmable quick patch: add a 250ms cooldown on kernel switches per GPU context and bump KV eviction threshold for tenants flagged as "hot". low-risk config change.
Priya: agree. also add a monitoring checkbox: emit kernel_switch_count per-tenant to help detection (currently we only have node-level metrics).
Devon: rolling a canary for the cooldown on pool-C now (config flip). will report after 2h.
Maya: for longer-term: consider per-tenant KV slot reservations and a reclaim policy (LRU per-tenant before global evict). that would preserve tail latency for stable tenants.
Ryan: +1. also need to add an integration test that simulates alternating seq lengths to catch selector regressions in CI.
Ilya: noted follow-ups:
- add per-tenant kernel_switch telemetry (pri=high)
- implement kernel cooldown (pri=high)
- experiment with partitioned KV cache prototype (pri=med)
- add CI harness for oscillating seq patterns (pri=med)

Priya: I've created a short runbook entry for oncall: how to spot kernel flip patterns, quick query examples, and immediate mitigation steps. link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kernel-flip (internal) :memo:
Devon: can we temporarily move heavy dev tenants off shared-pool-C to dedicated pools until we have the KV partitioning?
Ryan: ops, please coordinate migrations for flagged tenants and enforce QPS soft-limits on shared pools until cooldown is in prod.
Maya: thanks — will follow up once canary results are in. :thumbsup:
